native_result.HypoA: Higher time preference associated with higher BMI for 1989 data.
native_result.WorkflowA:
1. Selected appropriate variables from the raw data
e.g.: Height: Height of respondent on 1985 instead of 1981.
      Income: Total net family income, 1989 (There are many other income variables in the raw data)
      Age:    Age of respondent at 1989 (Derived from Age at 1979).
Data Transformation:
2. Replaced -1 to -5 values (unavailable data) with NaN
3. Imputed the missing values in the AGE and INCOME variable with mean.
4. AGE_1989 had missing values, hence derived the variable as [AGE_1979 + 10]
5. Created a BMI variable using: bmi = (weight) * 0.453592 / (height) * 0.0254
6. Divided the Family income variable by 1000$ (Mentioned in the paper)
7. Created an AGE^2 variable (From the paper)
8. One-hot encoded RACE variable into BLACK and HISPANIC
9. One-hot encooded GENDER variable into MALE and FEMALE
10. Selected 'Was more money put into or taken out of R/spouse savings since last interview, 1989' as the Time Preference variable.
  DISSAVED = 1 if 'TOOK MORE MONEY OUT' else 0
  SAMESAVE = 1 if 'NO SAVINGS' or 'NO CHANGE' else 0
11. Dropped the unimportant columns for replication
12. DISSAVED and SAMESAVE as independent variables and BMI as dependent variable
13. Fit an OLS Regression Model
native_result.HypoB: In NLSY79, higher time preference (present-biased savings flow 1985-89: took out or no savings vs put in) is associated with higher BMI: +0.143 BMI per present-bias point in 1989 (95% CI 0.063-0.223, n=10,167) and +0.186 in 1992 (0.088-0.285, n=8,322), adjusting for age, sex, race, income, wealth, education, ASVAB and incarceration; the raw saver vs non-saver gap (~0.9 BMI) is halved (~0.43) after adjustment. The association is a level difference (concentrated in women), not a differential 1981-1989 weight-gain effect (delta model n.s.), and persists 3 years after the savings window - directionally consistent with increased time preference leading to higher BMI, though the observational design supports association rather than proven causation.
native_result.WorkflowB: Inspected data (units: weights=lb, 1985 height=in, 1981 height excluded); built BMI_1981/1989/1992 from 1985 height, winsorized 1-99%; coded TP ordinal score from 1989 savings categorical; fitted OLS (HC1) primary (BMI_1989 ~ TP score, TP high, 4-dummy), secondary (BMI_1992, delta BMI + baseline), robustness (drop NO SAVINGS, sex-stratified, winsorization sensitivity, ordered logit on obesity category, listwise deletion, continuous net saving flow); compared raw vs adjusted magnitudes; added 1985-89 incarceration dummy to primary model.
